elements.element: Manufacture, package, label, or hold a dietary supplement
elements.quote: you are subject to this part if you manufacture, package, label, or hold a dietary supplement, including:

elements.element: includes those who hold for distribution
elements.quote: A dietary supplement you manufacture but that is packaged or labeled by another person; and
elements.note: Holding is covered generally by 111.1(a), but the enumerated inclusions are (1) supplements packaged/labeled by another person and (2) imported supplements; the text does not speak of 'hold for distribution'. J omits the import inclusion in (a)(2). Text not truncated.

elements.quote: do not apply to you if you are holding those dietary supplements at a retail establishment for the sole purpose of direct retail sale to individual consumers
elements.note: Exclusion is limited to the holding requirements only, and a retailer's warehouse is not a retail establishment.

rationale: Citation plainly governs, but J's 'includes those who hold for distribution' does not match the enumerated inclusions in 111.1(a)(1)-(2), and J omits the import inclusion.
uncertainty: An SME may consider 'hold for distribution' an acceptable paraphrase of 'hold' in 111.1(a).
needs_research_items: Decide whether J's 'hold for distribution' element is an acceptable paraphrase of 111.1(a) or should be flagged; J omits 111.1(a)(2) imports.

elements.quote: For the purpose of this part, the following definitions also apply:

elements.element: incorporates FD&C Act definitions by reference
elements.quote: The definitions and interpretations of terms in section 201 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the act) apply to such terms when used in this part.

elements.note: 111.3 text (not truncated) references only section 201 of the FD&C Act; no reference to 21 CFR Part 1 appears.

rationale: 111.3 incorporates FD&C Act section 201 definitions, but nothing in the evidence supports J's claim that Part 1 definitions are incorporated.
uncertainty: The 111.3 evidence text has garbled paragraph labels and ordering (e.g. microorganism sub-items appear at the top), so extraction problems cannot be ruled out.
needs_research_items: Verify whether any Part 111 provision incorporates 21 CFR Part 1 definitions; if not, the 'Part 1' element of J is wrong. Lead: 111.5 'Do other statutory provisions and regulations apply?' (heading only).
Check the 111.3 extraction against the eCFR source; paragraph labels appear scrambled.

elements.quote: You must have qualified employees who manufacture, package, label, or hold dietary supplements.
must have the education, training, or experience to perform the person's assigned functions

elements.note: Not in 111.12 (not truncated). The 111.13 text appears in this batch file under S-004 and states that qualified personnel must be assigned to supervise and that supervisors must be qualified by education, training, or experience.

completeness_note: The supervisor element is found only in 111.13, which G does not cite.
rationale: 111.12 supports the qualification and education/training/experience elements; the supervisor element is stated only in 111.13, whose text is in this batch's evidence (S-004 record).
evidence_refs: eCFR 21 CFR 111.13 (snapshot 2026-09-03; text carried in S-004 record)
uncertainty: The support for the correction comes from another row's record in the same batch file. An SME might also decide the question needs only 111.12 and that J's supervisor element goes beyond it.

elements.note: 111.13 covers only supervisors; text not truncated.

completeness_note: The cited section is headed 'What supervisor requirements apply?' and does not address hygienic practices.
rationale: 111.13 addresses supervisor qualifications, not employee hygiene; none of the J elements appear in it. The likely governing section's text is not in the evidence, so a correction cannot be proposed from evidence.
needs_research_items: Retrieve the 21 CFR 111.10 text (heading: 'What requirements apply for preventing microbial contamination from sick or infected personnel and for hygienic practices?') and confirm it states each J element; if so, correct G to 21 CFR 111.10.

elements.quote: You must make and keep records required under this subpart B in accordance with subpart P of this part.
elements.note: 111.14(b) lists the records: written procedures and training documentation.

elements.element: plus Subpart P general records/retention rules
elements.quote: You must keep written records required by this part for 1 year past the shelf life date, if shelf life dating is used, or 2 years beyond the date of distribution of the last batch
elements.note: 111.610 adds FDA availability requirements.

rationale: 111.14 states the subpart B records and routes them to subpart P, and 111.605/111.610 give the general retention, form, and availability rules.
uncertainty: That 111.605 and 111.610 make up the whole of subpart P is inferred from the same_subpart listing; J is terse.

elements.quote: removing litter and waste
elements.note: Also 111.15(j) trash disposal.

elements.quote: You must take effective measures to exclude pests from the physical plant
You must maintain your physical plant in a clean and sanitary condition
You must use cleaning compounds and sanitizing agents that are free from microorganisms of public health significance
You must provide your employees with adequate, readily accessible bathrooms.
The plumbing in your physical plant must be of an adequate size and design and be adequately installed and maintained to:

rationale: Every J element is stated in 111.15, which is the section on physical plant and grounds sanitation.

elements.element: Water that contacts components/product or contact surfaces must be safe and sanitary quality
elements.note: 111.16 only requires written procedures for cleaning and pest control (not truncated). Water supply requirements are in 111.15(e), whose text appears in this batch under S-006: (e)(1) requires safe and sanitary water where water does not become a component; (e)(2) requires water that contacts components, supplements, or contact surfaces to comply with Federal, State, and local requirements and not contaminate the supplement.

completeness_note: The cited section does not govern water supply; 111.15(e) does.
rationale: 111.16 concerns written procedures for cleaning and pest control; the water supply requirements are in 111.15(e), whose text is in this batch's evidence (S-006 record).
evidence_refs: eCFR 21 CFR 111.15(e) (snapshot 2026-09-03; text carried in S-006 record)
uncertainty: Even under 111.15(e), J blurs the two tiers: the 'safe and sanitary' standard in (e)(1) applies to water that does not become a component, while water contacting components or contact surfaces must meet Federal/State/local requirements under (e)(2). J itself cannot be corrected through this system.
needs_research_items: The SME should decide whether J's wording is acceptable given the (e)(1)/(e)(2) distinction; 111.365(c) (in S-023 record) also addresses water that may become a component.

elements.quote: Be suitable in size, construction, and design to facilitate maintenance, cleaning, and sanitizing operations;
separate or defined areas of adequate size or other control systems, such as computerized inventory controls or automated systems of separation, to prevent contamination and mixups
Provide adequate light in:
Adequate ventilation or environmental control equipment such as airflow systems, including filters, fans, and other air-blowing equipment
Floors, walls, and ceilings that can be adequately cleaned and kept clean and in good repair;

rationale: Every J element is stated in 111.20, the design and construction section.

elements.quote: Establish and use appropriate controls to ensure that the equipment functions in accordance with its intended use.
elements.note: 111.30(a) requires designing or selecting equipment to meet specifications; installation is not mentioned.

elements.quote: Routinely calibrate, inspect, or check the equipment to ensure proper performance.

elements.note: No backup requirement in 111.30; text not truncated.

elements.quote: ensure that any changes to the manufacturing, packaging, labeling, holding, or other operations are approved by quality control personnel and instituted only by authorized personnel

completeness_note: The backup element may reside in a records provision not cited, but the evidence does not show it.
rationale: Calibration and change-control elements are supported, but 111.30 does not mention backup or installation.
needs_research_items: Locate any backup requirement for computerized equipment. Lead: 111.35 'Under this subpart D, what records must you make and keep?' (heading only); add it to G if it contains the backup requirement.

elements.element: Establish and follow written procedures covering all stages of manufacturing, packaging, labeling, holding
elements.quote: You must implement a system of production and process controls that covers all stages of manufacturing, packaging, labeling, and holding of the dietary supplement
elements.note: 111.55 requires implementing a system; it does not mention written procedures (not truncated).

rationale: 111.55 supports the 'all stages' system requirement, but not J's 'written procedures' framing.
needs_research_items: Identify the subpart E written-procedures provision (lead: 111.53, from general knowledge; not in evidence) and decide whether J's 'written procedures' element should cite it.

elements.quote: For each component that you use in the manufacture of a dietary supplement, you must establish component specifications as follows:
You must establish in-process specifications for any point, step, or stage in the master manufacturing record where control is necessary
You must establish specifications for dietary supplement labels (label specifications) and for packaging that may come in contact with dietary supplements (packaging specifications).
you must establish product specifications for the identity, purity, strength, and composition of the finished batch of the dietary supplement
If you receive a product from a supplier for packaging or labeling as a dietary supplement (and for distribution rather than for return to the supplier), you must establish specifications

rationale: 111.70 is the governing section and states every J category.
uncertainty: J omits 111.70(a), specifications at any control point, and 111.70(g), specifications for finished packaging and labeling. The citation is right, but a strict SME may consider J incomplete.

elements.quote: You must determine whether the specifications you establish under § 111.70 are met.

elements.element: quality control personnel material review and disposition
elements.quote: Quality control personnel must conduct all required material reviews and make all required disposition decisions.
Detect any deviation or unanticipated occurrence that may result in a failure to meet specifications.
elements.note: The cited text covers detecting deviations, plus conditions on treatment and reprocessing in 111.90, which says those actions must be 'permitted by § 111.77'. What a firm must do when a spec is not met is under 111.77, which is not cited and not in the evidence.

elements.quote: You must not reprocess a rejected dietary supplement or treat or provide an in-process adjustment to a component, packaging, or label
elements.note: 111.90(c) also requires QC approval and compliance with 111.123(b) before release.

completeness_note: 111.90(a)(2) and (b)(2) route expressly to § 111.77 ('What must you do if established specifications are not met?'), which G omits.
rationale: The cited sections support the determination, QC disposition, and reprocessing-limit elements, but the cited text routes the core 'what to do when a spec fails' question to 111.77, whose text is not in the evidence.
needs_research_items: Retrieve the 111.77 text and confirm it governs the action required when a finished-batch identity specification fails; if so, add 21 CFR 111.77 to G.
Lead: 111.113 'What quality control operations are required for a material review and disposition decision?' (heading only).

elements.element: Representative samples of components, packaging, labels
elements.quote: Representative samples of each unique lot of components, packaging, and labels that you use
Representative samples of in-process materials for each manufactured batch
Representative samples of a subset of finished batches of each dietary supplement that you manufacture
Consist of at least twice the quantity necessary for all tests or examinations to determine whether or not the dietary supplement meets product specifications.
Be held using the same container-closure system in which the packaged and labeled dietary supplement is distributed
elements.note: 111.83 addresses the container-closure system, not storage conditions such as environment (not truncated).

elements.quote: Be retained for 1 year past the shelf life date (if shelf life dating is used), or for 2 years from the date of distribution of the last batch

rationale: All elements are supported except 'storage conditions', where 111.83 speaks only of the container-closure system.
uncertainty: An SME may accept the container-closure requirement as 'storage conditions'.
needs_research_items: Check whether reserve-sample holding conditions are set elsewhere (lead from general knowledge: 111.465, holding of reserve samples; not in evidence) and whether G should include it.

elements.quote: Approving or rejecting all processes, specifications, written procedures, controls, tests, and examinations
Reviewing and approving the documentation setting forth the basis for qualification of any supplier;
elements.note: 111.105(b)-(e) cover reviewing specific documentation; general record review, such as batch records, is not stated in 111.105.
Not stated in 111.105 (only '(i) Performing other operations required under this subpart'). 111.87 text (in S-012 record) states it.

elements.quote: and deviations from or modifications to them, that may affect the identity, purity, strength, or composition of a dietary supplement
elements.note: Deviations are covered; reprocessing approval is not in 111.105 (it is in 111.90, carried in the S-012 record).

completeness_note: The material review/disposition and reprocessing elements are found only in provisions G does not cite (111.87 and 111.90 in this batch; 111.113 and 111.123 are heading-only leads).
rationale: 111.105 supports approval/rejection and deviations, but material review/disposition and reprocessing approval appear only in uncited provisions, and the subpart F sections that may govern are not in evidence.
needs_research_items: Retrieve 111.113 (QC operations for material review and disposition) and 111.123 (QC operations for MMR/BPR) and decide whether G should cite them, or 111.87/111.90, for the material review, record review and reprocessing elements.

elements.quote: have distinct and separate responsibilities related to performing such operations from those responsibilities that the person otherwise has when not performing such operations
elements.note: The text requires separate responsibilities, not 'independence' as such.

elements.quote: Approving or rejecting all processes, specifications, written procedures, controls, tests, and examinations
You must identify who is responsible for your quality control operations.
elements.note: Read with the distinct-and-separate-responsibilities sentence in 111.12(b).
No such prohibition in either cited text (neither truncated).

rationale: The cited provisions support QC approval authority and separate responsibilities, but not an express 'no self-approval' rule; 'independence' goes beyond the text.
uncertainty: 'No self-approval' may be an interpretive gloss (e.g. from preamble or guidance) rather than regulatory text.
needs_research_items: Determine whether any Part 111 provision prohibits QC personnel approving their own work; if none exists, the J element is unsupported.

elements.note: Not in the cited sections (not truncated). Identity testing appears in 111.75(a)(1)-(2), whose text is in this batch under S-012 and S-017.
Not in the cited sections. COA conditions are in 111.75(a)(2)(ii), carried in the S-012 and S-017 records.

elements.quote: You must quarantine components before you use them in the manufacture of a dietary supplement until:
elements.note: Also 111.160(c) for packaging and labels.

elements.quote: the status of the component (e.g., quarantined, approved, or rejected)
elements.note: Rejected status is mentioned only as a traceability field; handling of rejected materials is not stated.

completeness_note: Two J elements are found only in 111.75(a), which G does not cite. The rejection element may be governed by 111.170 (heading only).
rationale: The cited sections support quarantine but not identity testing or COA conditions. Those are in 111.75(a), which appears elsewhere in this batch, while the rejection element's likely governing section is not in evidence.
needs_research_items: Likely correction: add 21 CFR 111.75(a) to G (supported by the evidence in this batch).
Retrieve 111.170 (rejected components, packaging, and labels) and confirm whether it governs the rejection element.

elements.element: Identity test of a dietary ingredient by the manufacturer is required
elements.quote: Conduct at least one appropriate test or examination to verify the identity of any component that is a dietary ingredient, unless you petition the agency under paragraph (a)(1)(ii)
elements.note: The requirement is subject to an FDA petition exemption under (a)(1)(ii), which J omits.

elements.element: COA reliance permitted for other component specs
elements.quote: Rely on a certificate of analysis from the supplier of the component that you receive, provided that:
elements.note: (a)(2) applies this to confirming the identity of other components and other component specifications.

elements.quote: You first qualify the supplier by establishing the reliability of the supplier's certificate of analysis through confirmation of the results of the supplier's tests or examinations;
You periodically re-confirm the supplier's certificate of analysis; and
elements.note: J omits conditions (B) COA content, (C) documentation, and (E) QC approval.

completeness_note: 111.155 adds little to the COA question, but its inclusion is not wrong.
rationale: The citation governs and the COA conditions are supported, but J states identity testing of dietary ingredients as absolute, while the text allows an FDA-granted petition exemption.
uncertainty: An SME may deem the petition exemption immaterial to the question as posed.
needs_research_items: SME to decide whether J's unqualified 'identity test ... is required' is acceptable given the 111.75(a)(1)(ii) petition exemption, and whether omitting COA conditions (B), (C), and (E) matters.

elements.quote: The name of the dietary supplement to be manufactured and the strength, concentration, weight, or measure of each dietary ingredient for each batch size;
of each dietary ingredient for each batch size;
A complete list of components to be used;
An accurate statement of the weight or measure of each component to be used;
The identity and weight or measure of each dietary ingredient that will be declared on the Supplement Facts label
Procedures for sampling and a cross-reference to procedures for tests or examinations;
Specifications for each point, step, or stage in the manufacturing process where control is necessary to ensure the quality of the dietary supplement
Specific actions necessary to perform and verify points, steps, or stages in the manufacturing process where control is necessary
elements.note: Paraphrase.

elements.quote: A description of packaging and a representative label

rationale: 111.210 is the governing section and states every J element.
uncertainty: Some elements are paraphrased ('in-process controls'). J omits overage (e), theoretical yield (f), and corrective action plans. The 111.210 extraction also mislabels sub-paragraphs under (h)(3).

elements.element: MMR required for each unique formulation and batch size
elements.quote: You must prepare and follow a written master manufacturing record for each unique formulation of dietary supplement that you manufacture, and for each batch size

elements.element: BPR must accurately follow the MMR
elements.quote: Your batch production record must accurately follow the appropriate master manufacturing record

rationale: Both J elements are stated verbatim in the two cited sections, which govern MMRs and BPRs respectively.

elements.quote: The batch, lot, or control number:
The identity and weight or measure of each component used;
The date on which each step of the master manufacturing record was performed; and
elements.note: 111.260(c) also requires the date and time of equipment maintenance, cleaning, and sanitizing.

elements.quote: The identity of equipment and processing lines used in producing the batch;

elements.element: initials of persons performing and verifying
elements.quote: The initials of the person responsible for verifying the weight or measure of each component used in the batch;
The results of any testing or examination performed during the batch production, or a cross-reference to such results;
Documentation at the time of performance of any required material review and disposition decision.
elements.note: 111.260 requires documenting material review/disposition and reprocessing; 'deviations' as such are not named (not truncated).

rationale: All elements but one are directly stated; 'documentation of deviations' matches only indirectly through the material review/disposition documentation in 111.260(m).
uncertainty: An SME may accept 111.260(m) as covering deviations, since deviations trigger material review.
needs_research_items: Confirm that 'documentation of deviations' is adequately represented by 111.260(m)-(n), or flag the J wording.

elements.note: 111.310 covers only laboratory facilities (not truncated).

completeness_note: The cited section is headed 'What are the requirements for the laboratory facilities that you use?'; the question asks about laboratory control processes.
rationale: 111.310 concerns adequate laboratory facilities and states none of the J elements; the likely governing section's text is not in the evidence.
needs_research_items: Retrieve the 21 CFR 111.315 text (heading: 'What are the requirements for laboratory control processes?') and confirm it states each J element; if so, correct G to 21 CFR 111.315.

elements.element: Methods must be appropriate and scientifically valid
elements.quote: You must identify and use an appropriate scientifically valid method for each established specification

elements.element: verification of suitability for the matrix
elements.quote: You must verify that the laboratory examination and testing methodologies are appropriate for their intended use.
elements.note: The text requires verification for 'intended use'; the word 'matrix' does not appear (not truncated).

rationale: The citation governs, and the scientifically valid method element is supported. 'Suitability for the matrix' is narrower than the text's 'appropriate for their intended use'.
uncertainty: An SME may treat 'matrix' as a reasonable gloss on 'intended use'.
needs_research_items: SME to decide whether 'suitability for the matrix' is an acceptable paraphrase of 111.320(a).

elements.quote: Cleaning and sanitizing contact surfaces;
elements.note: Given only as an example for mechanical manufacturing steps. General sanitation for manufacturing operations may be in 111.360 (heading only).

elements.quote: You must take all the necessary precautions during the manufacture of a dietary supplement to prevent contamination of components or dietary supplements.
Using effective measures to protect against the inclusion of metal or other foreign material in components or dietary supplements
Performing chemical, microbiological, or other testing, as necessary to prevent the use of contaminated components;
Performing manufacturing operations under conditions and controls that protect against the potential for growth of microorganisms and the potential for contamination;

completeness_note: Possible omission of 111.360 for sanitation, but only its heading is in evidence, so this is not flagged as an omission.
rationale: 111.365 supports the contamination-prevention and hazard-control elements. The general 'sanitation' element is only incidentally supported and may belong to 111.360.
uncertainty: An SME may accept 111.365(h)(1) as sufficient for 'sanitation'.
needs_research_items: Retrieve 111.360 ('What are the requirements for sanitation?') and decide whether G should add it for the sanitation element.
